page.layout: Running head at top centre, with the page number at top left. Below it, two medallion engravings side by side (left: Emanuel Philibert; right: Margaret of Valois), with their legends inside the rings. Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs, full width, no margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.p: PHILIBERTVS Emanuel Dux Sabaudiæ & princeps Pedemōtanus, amisso eius dominio, quod Rex Gallorum Henricus 2. obtinebat, diutissime pro Carolo quinto Imperatore, aduersus ipsum Henricum dimicauit. Quid is egerit, præfectus Imperatoris exercitui, in obsidione Hesdini, satis notum est ex historia bellorum quæ inter hos duos potentissimos principes, totius prope orbis detrimento, gesta sunt. Huius pater Carolus Dux Sabaudiæ, propriis sedibus & toto suo dominio expulsus, mortuus est anno salutis 1553. éstque sepultus Vercelliis. Post eius obitum Imperator Carolus dedit Philiberto Emanueli, paterna hereditate destituto, Comitatum Astensem, vt eo potiretur donec suam hæreditatem recuperasset, quę illi postea fuit restituta omnino à Rege, qui etiā dedit illi nuptui sororē suam vnicam Margaretam, Francisci 1. Francorum regis filiam, quæ paulo post Henrici tertij è Polonia reditum in Galliam, fatis cessit, magno omniū luctu, & præcipuè Ducis qui celebrē illam Augustæ Taurinorum Academiā, in studioforum vsum instituit.

MARGARETA Valesia, Heroinarum omnium quotquot fuerunt longè illustrissima, pietate ac in omnes literatos homines præcipuè Gallos humanitate ac liberalitate valde insignis, Christianissimi & inuictissimi illius Henrici secundi soror vnica, Philiberto Emanuelî gloriosissimo Sabaudiæ principi, nupsit eodem tempore quo Elizabetha Franciæ filia natu maior, collocata est in matrimonium Philippo regi Hispaniæ, quorum Hymenæorum ratione, pax sancita & confirmata fuit inter Imperatorem, Regem Hispaniæ, & Christianissimum Francorum regem Henricum. Hæc sanè digna est, propter eius virtutes infinitas, quę ęuo omniū scriptis cumulatissimè celebretur.

page.notes: Two medallion engravings at the top are illustrations, not transcribed as text. Left medal legend, as far as legible: "EMANVEL. PHILIB." and "D. SABAVDIÆ". Right medal legend, partly worn: "MARGARITA DE" and "VALESIA D. SABAVD" [?]. The words "PHILIBERTVS" and "MARGARETA" open their paragraphs in capitals and are copied as running text. Some letters in the medal legends are doubtful. The spelling "Pedemōtanus" uses a tilde over the o as printed.
